tone_statements.citation: Andargachew Getu Gebeyehu. 2021. Documentation and grammatical description of Gwama. PhD dissertation, Addis Ababa University. 310 pp.
tone_statements.quote: In Gwama, pitch variation of sounds differentiate the meanings of words. To this end, like other Nilo-Saharan languages, Gwama is a tonal language. The tone bearing units of the language are vowels. … In this study, three contrastive tone levels (High (H), Mid (M), and Low (L)) are identified. High tone is represented by (V́), mid tone without any mark as (V), and low tone by (V̀ )20. The following examples of minimal pairs show the three contrastive level tones of the language. … the Gwama tone indicates that it has lexical and grammatical functions. That is, tone in Gwama is phonemic.
tone_statements.locator: sec. 2.4 Tone and 2.4.1 Lexical Function, pp. 67-69; minimal pairs/triplets ex. 66-77, grammatical tone ex. 78 (p. 70)

tone_statements.citation: Küspert, Klaus-Christian. 2015. The Mao and Komo languages in the Begi-Tongo area in Western Ethiopia: classification, designations, distribution. Linguistic Discovery 13(1): 1-63.
tone_statements.quote: According to Anne-Christie Hellenthal (p.c.), there are a couple of morphologic and tone differences besides the already mentioned phonetic differences and some rather well known varieties in the vocabulary. The morphologic differences concerning topics such as the systems of personal pronouns would need further investigation, as well as the partial (?) loss of tone distinctions in Koman Mao.

sources.note: Nothing. Dedicated 27-pp phonology (consonants, vowels, ATR harmony, length, sec. 4 Tone pp. 374-375: three contrastive level tones H/M/L, noun and verb melodies; sec. 5 syllable structure; morphophonemics). The word 'stress' does not occur; no statement on accent/prominence.

sources.citation: Otero, Manuel A. 2019. A historical reconstruction of the Koman language family. PhD dissertation, University of Oregon. 756 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Gwama phonological sketch sec. 2.1.4 (pp. 40-47, Highland and Lowland Gwama, own fieldwork + Hellenthal & Kutsch Lojenga 2011, Goldberg et al. 2017); sec. 2.1.4.4 'Gwama Tone' p. 47: three level tones L/M/H plus rising; 'no significant tonal processes.. nor is there downstepping or downdrifting'.
